A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaussian Mapping for Evolving Scenes (GaME). All supplied pages, figures, tables and equations are readable, including v1 Appendix A. Its experiments can be matched to their relocated counterparts in v2 despite substantial method and layout revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original rendering experiments on Flat, Aria and TUM-RGBD, component ablations, and noisy-pose and runtime results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark, ablation, noisy-pose and runtime results, plus a new hyperparameter sensitivity experiment in Table 9.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 substantially revise scene adaptation. V2 removes the Add mask-overlap gate, explicitly reinitializes conflicting Gaussians, and changes new-region seeding from low opacity AND a fixed depth-error threshold to low opacity OR above-median depth error. Panoptic-mask overlap tests are replaced by SAM masks and FlashSplat assignment for removal, with SAM-based keyframe masking and revised keyframe exclusion.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Flat sequences, two changing Aria rooms, three static TUM-RGBD scenes, and estimated-pose conditions on Aria room0. The new sensitivity experiment uses existing dataset coverage; its inconsistent dataset identification does not establish an added domain or task.

E2.justification: Flat, Aria and runtime comparisons retain SplaTAM, MonoGS and DG-SLAM; static-scene comparisons retain SplaTAM and MonoGS. Wild-GS remains excluded for the same stated reasons. SAM and FlashSplat are method components, not added evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new sensitivity protocol varies depth, color and opacity thresholds by −20%, −10%, +10% and +20%. Its dataset is inconsistently identified as Flat in Section 5.2 and Aria room0 in Table 9. Existing benchmarks retain full-resolution rendering, ground-truth poses, every-tenth-frame novel-view holdout and the stated static-scene protocol.

E4.justification: V2 Table 9 adds an analysis of rendering sensitivity to three detection thresholds. DSA, keyframe-filtering, refinement and noisy-pose analyses remain, with revised outcomes. The noisy-pose study was already present in v1 Appendix A and is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 Table 9 introduces means and standard deviations across hyperparameter perturbations, whereas v1 reports point estimates. These describe parameter sensitivity; neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised. Flat input/novel depth error changes from 16.63/15.59 to 6.9/7.9 cm; estimated-pose Aria depth changes from 3.6/3.6 to 0.70/0.70 cm. TUM average PSNR falls from 21.15 to 20.63, while reported GaME FPS rises from 0.165 to 0.52 and DG-SLAM FPS changes from 0.346 to 0.25. Table 4 now gives no filtering lower depth error than partial filtering, reversing v1. These are revised-system results, with unchanged nominal settings not established.

T1.justification: Formal selection definitions change: v1 Equation (7)'s conjunction and fixed threshold become a disjunction and median threshold in v2 Equation (8), while the keyframe removal-region inequalities reverse between v1 Equation (11) and v2 Equation (10). The background 3DGS mathematics remains substantially unchanged, and neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central first-system claim and the DSA/keyframe-management contributions remain. Quantitative headline claims strengthen from 90+% depth and 20+% color improvement to approximately 29.7% PSNR and over threefold depth improvement against competitive baselines; v2's introduction separately states 325% depth improvement.

C2.justification: V2 explains SAM masks as overlapping, label-free object silhouettes and attributes multiview robustness to FlashSplat. It adds an interpretation that threshold sensitivity is low and identifies retaining a complete 4D change history as future work. The earlier semantic-mask noise limitation disappears; the non-real-time qualification survives in Section 5.2.

D1.justification: V1 Appendix Table 7 supplies dataset-specific loss weights, detection thresholds and keyframe settings for Flat and Aria. V2 removes this table without replacement numerical defaults, providing qualitative tuning guidance and relative perturbations instead. Explicit masked-loss formulas and the explanation for dropping SSIM are also omitted. The RTX 3090 disclosure and project/code-release statements remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to SAM, FlashSplat, MASt3R-SLAM and Dynamic and Deformable SLAM, and removes Mask DINO. These update implementation attribution and introductory context; the related-work categories and positioning against offline change detection and short-term dynamic mapping remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The introduction is reframed around outdated geometry and stale observations, and the method exposition is extensively rewritten. Appendix A's noisy-pose, runtime and baseline discussions are integrated into the main experimental narrative, while its implementation table disappears. The limitations and performance summaries are also revised.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column format with a two-column layout, adds an overview Figure 1 and masked-keyframe Figure 4, and enlarges or relocates retained illustrations. Tables are redistributed into narrower columns; the appendix settings table is removed and a new sensitivity table added. These are substantial visual and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 adds sensitivity evidence, useful visual explanations and a substantive method revision with better reported evolving-scene geometry and runtime. However, it removes reproducibility-critical numerical settings and explicit masking-loss details. New reporting conflicts weaken confidence: Section 5.2 and Table 9 disagree on the sensitivity dataset, and Table 2's novel-view PSNR average of 31.23 is below both listed room scores, 31.48 and 31.97. These gains and documentation weaknesses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
